pages.text: Light climbing a height H in gravity g loses a fraction gH/c² of its frequency. The gamma ray of iron-57 is so sharp that this shift - a few parts in 10¹⁵ - can be seen: move the source up at v = gH/c and the Doppler shift cancels it. Counting N gamma rays measures the line's centre to its width over √N. A temperature difference between source and absorber shifts it too, by 2.2×10⁻¹⁵ a kelvin.
$(thing)Set$(): Source speed v, Counting time.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Vibration of the tower: the thermal shift wanders by ±10%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): none beyond the recipe windows.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Shorter counts are faster; a taller tower measures more at once.

$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Tower height: H = 7.5 m · storeys$(br)Gravitational shift: Δf/f = gH/c²$(br)Speed that cancels it: v = gH/c$(br)Thermal shift: Δv = 0.66 µm/s per K$(br)Counting error: σ = Γ/√N$(br)Mistuning: |v − v_g − v_th|/σ$(br)Significance: v_g/σ
